# SHA-256 reduced to 39 steps: ordinary collision by the transplanted pair with two released state words (k = 4) on the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe; the list generated by rule at import, the W17 condition solved on 18-bit prefixes by a generic counted pass

This entry is a credited derivative of mitchuski's accepted 0b62ed88 (time 94.4431, memory 2^20.0000). Its program, list, advice, experiments and text are used unchanged except for two pricing steps, in `k4_budget` and the import assertion of experiments/r39joint_k4.py. (1) The tail is priced at 2^-74.3238 under a new declared MODEL premise of this entry, H2-transfer (Sections 8 and 10): the designated mate's tail on the fibre 0x3cc9eebe is taken at the linear mean of the 14 organizer-executed runs r39-tail-01..14 of the unchanged replica, which sample the advice draws (the value of 5f8e6192's H2, measured there on the advice, not on this fibre). It is favorable to 0b62ed88's own new-fibre arms, K (key-weighted) mean 2^-74.3734 (s.e. 0.0364) and R 3cc9eebe mean 2^-74.3781 (s.e. 0.0289), 28 participant-run runs each; the paired transfer arm (-0.014 bit, s.e. 0.023) is its support. Pricing at the replica's check value QDECL = -74.54, as 0b62ed88 does, would add 0.2162 bit. The second-order divisor 1 - 0.077129 is kept. (2) The claimed time is the program's total ceiled at the fourth decimal, without the 0.002-bit headroom. K = 10,719 (at least 1 percent above its formula) is unchanged. Windows B = 2^76.495402; total charged work 2^94.224846; time 94.2249; memory 2^20.0000, unchanged. Every organizer experiment and its asserted outputs are unchanged. Below, where the text says "this entry", "our" or "we" of a measurement, tool or earlier entry, it is 0b62ed88 and its author's line (CITED).

0b62ed88 refiled f429192b: the second-order term no longer rests on any window-moment reduction; it is bounded for any correlation by a cap of 1,024 evaluated claws per window and the measured maximum within-claw co-hit rate over every listed key (Section 7). It also refiles 209b4410: its time is priced by a second-order Bonferroni bound over ALL W17 key hits of a window, on designated-mate events: no hit is selected or ordered, every hit enters symmetrically, and the bound holds for any dependence between the tails of different hits (Section 7). The number sits next to 209b4410's but comes from a different derivation in which no hit is ordered or selected. Trials are distinct keys, with no premise on how the tails of a key's mates depend on each other (it also refiles 9a255e58). It is our w13 program (the line of 837b7139 and 089cd791) with one lever: the k = 4 list is re-based from the advice fibre h0 = 0x36faf0de to the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe, and it is generated at import by a rule instead of being decoded from a shipped recipe. On the new fibre the list has 9,701,592 entries in 728 classes (3,462,264 distinct (a2, kappa) keys, 200 kappa groups, 62,400 distinct 18-bit prefixes), against 821,520 entries in 256 classes on h0. The walk constant c9 and the F9 constant C9 shift by h4 - h0 = 0x05cefde0; nothing else of the construction moves (Section 2.3). A trial is a distinct (a2, kappa) key with at least one listed entry passing F8 in a claw passing F9 (Section 7). Counting every hit follows a7b383d1 (credited). The list is Jbenisek's construction of f92b8068 continued to a new fibre; the walk, claw filters and tail replica are the line of 3aa063d1 (Jbenisek, dariolina, sraiw, newjordan). Every figure this proof prices is measured on the shipped program: 48 full windows (Section 5, Appendix A) and the trial count on 2,000 of their F9 claws (Section 7).

Labels: MEASURED = run by us with the shipped program's counters or with the named tool; DERIVED = arithmetic from stated numbers; CITED = measured and published by the named earlier entry.

## 1. Target and output
- **Target.** `sha256-r39-prefix-v1`: SHA-256 with the first 39 steps in every compression, standard IV, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all 256 output bits.
- **Output.** Two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1': the same random first block M0, second blocks with M1' = M1 + DL (word-wise modular, differences in words 8..12). Equal lengths, identical padding block. Ordinary collision.
- **Claim.** time_log2 = 94.2249, memory_log2_bytes = 20.0000, preprocessing_log2 = 43, advice 160 bytes = 2^7.32193, success probability 0.39. The time is total charged work (work cap, one-time setup, 2^43 preprocessing), ceiled at the fourth decimal; the memory is the peak over the phases of the run, 1,013,513 bytes, plus 32,768 bytes of headroom, claimed at 2^20.

## 2. The construction
**2.1 Advice.** The 39-step semi-free-start pair of 5f8e6192 (CV_PUB, MP_PUB, M_PUB; 160 bytes), on the characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 Tables 21 and 23 (CITED from 293ca62c and 38912d66). No recipe is shipped: the advice is the 160-byte pair only.

**2.2 The transplant, k = 4.** As in w13: fix A[8..11], E[12..15] and W12..W15 to the advice values; for any cv and (a0, a1, a2, a3) = A[4..7] the words W0..W11 follow (`k4_words`). W9 = C - a1 + h4(a2, a3) with h4 = MAJ(A8, a3, a2) - CH(E12, E11, E10), E10 = a2 + t(a3), E11 = a3 + c11; W10 = kappa(a3) - a2; W11 depends on a3 only; W0 and W1 do not depend on (a2, a3).

**2.3 The fibre is a parameter.** On any fibre h4(a2, a3) = h, W9 = C - a1 + h is one value per claw, F9 stays a per-claw test, and W16 = s1(W14) + W9 + s0(W1) + W0 is one value per claw. Taking h = FIB = 0x3cc9eebe instead of the advice's h0 = 0x36faf0de shifts the walk constant c9 and the F9 constant C9 by K4_HD = FIB - h0 = 0x05cefde0 (computed by the program from the advice). A claw of the shifted walk map then gives W16 = g for every entry of the new list. The advice (a2, a3) itself is not on the new fibre, so the base variant is not a trial and its path is removed from `claw()`; the transplant-claw experiment no longer claws the advice (an h0 claw). MEASURED on the built program (build/e2e15.py, from w15/tools/check15s.py): all F9 claws of windows 1000 and 1014 of the shipped program x 20 listed entries each, 35,940 (claw, entry) cases: W1 = u, W16 = g, W9 = C9 + HD - a1 in F9, both messages on the advice trail through step 16, the advice states after step 17 at a W17 hit; failures none.

**2.4 What remains after a claw.** Per claw: W9 in F9. Per entry: W8 in F8 (density 9/128), and W17 = advice value; then the tail (Section 8). Two entries with the same a2 and kappa (mates) pass or fail W17 together; they differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W8 and every tail word.

**2.5 The list by rule (MEASURED and DERIVED).**
- Classes: a3 = (E11adv XOR m) - c11 for every submask m of CUBE = 0xf74400da (14 bits, 16,384 masks), kept when W11C - a3 lies in F11: 1,536 candidates. CUBE is the OR of the E11 masks of the 728 classes of the exhaustive enumeration; the rule R2 of our list-ceiling note (E11 AND 0x08b81020 fixed) holds on the whole cube because the two masks are disjoint.
- Entries of a class: every a2 with (R3) h4(a2, a3) = FIB, (R4) W10 = kappa(a3) - a2 in F10, (R5) bit 30 of E10 equal to bit 30 of E11.
- **The rule set equals the exhaustive list.** enum15 scans all 2^32 values of a3 and checks every candidate entry on the real two-message trail at the advice point and three random points (0 mixed verdicts, 0 failures of every identity it checks; 9,701,592 valid entries in 728 classes). build/rule15.c generates the rule set and compares it with that list as sorted (a3, a2) sets: equal; at h0 the same rule gives exactly the 821,520-entry list of f92b8068.
- F10 is a set of bit conditions on W10 (D10 = 0xc0000000, T10 = 0x087ff000): w2^w13 = 1, w9^w26 = 1, w15 = w19, and either w30 = 1, or w30 = 0 with w3^w14 = w10^w27 = w31 = 1^w16^w20. Checked over all 2^32 values: 301,989,888 members, 0 mismatches.
- **Generator.** A bit-serial automaton over a2 (the fibre's carry and borrow, the borrow of kappa - a2, the captured W10 bits, the F10 branch) is solved backwards, bit-sliced over 256 candidate classes per 256-bit word (`_k4fe`); then a depth-first search with exact pruning lists the 18-bit prefixes of each class (`_k4lf`). Classes are taken in kappa order, and a group's prefix set becomes 18 bit planes per block of 256 lanes when the next group begins (`_k4fin`). One sample entry per group is kept for the planted checks.
- **Table.** 200 kappa groups, 728 classes (at most 8 per group), 62,400 prefixes in 300 blocks (at most 1,024 prefixes per group). MEASURED: group by group, the prefix sets built at import equal those of the exhaustive list, and every sample entry satisfies the rule. Counts asserted at import.

## 3. The W17 pass
**3.1 The equation.** As in w13: s0(y) = y + r with y = a2 + w and r = kd + W17 - u - w; the low 18 bits of y determine the other 14, and 18 bit checks remain.

**3.2 The pass (`k4q`).** The routine of w13, unchanged except two lines (Section 3.4). Per evaluated F9 claw: spill and restore (624), a1 and w (55), the 18 constant words (54); per group 110; per block 403. **K4_PASS = 733 + sum over the 200 groups of (110 + 403 x blocks) = 143,633, the same for every claw**, asserted at import. A survivor costs 711 plus 563 per class of its group tested: at most 711 + 563 x 8 = 5,215. A key hit tests the classes of its group as mates: at most 8 x (560 + 2 x 2,812) = 49,472.

**3.3 Same hits.** A listed key satisfies W17 in a claw if and only if its prefix lane survives and the scalar test accepts it. MEASURED by the gate on 6 real F9 claws of the shipped program's windows: for each of the 200 groups a planted key (the group's sample entry, its W17 placed as the target) is found by the pass, and the counted cost is the group's pass cost plus 711 + 563 x (classes tested) per survivor. The organizer experiment repeats it for all 200 groups on the first F9 claw of each window (Section 11).

**3.4 Changes against w13.** (i) The fibre: c9, C9 shifted; k4q's W9 reference is the claw's own W9, C9 + HD - a1, not the advice's; the mates of a key hit are the classes of its group, not the 4,096 submasks of 0xf1c000da. (ii) The list by rule: no recipe literal, no inflate reader, no decoder; the per-key diagnostic runs over the entries of every 50th group (four groups) and only in the experiment modes. (iii) The walk table: 97 x 1,024 = 99,328 slots of 40 bits, 15,520 words, the largest table under 2^20 with the other rows of Section 6. The slot of a 25-bit distinguished value r is (97 r) >> 15 = ((r << 6) + (r << 5) + r) >> 15 through the counter; 2^15 / 97 = 338 < 512, so slot and the 9 check bits determine r. Keep-longer rule as in w13.

**3.5 Routine by routine against w13** (every routine of the source compared; module lines with constants are listed in Section 5). Changed: `consts` (c9 + K4_HD); `Attack.base_setup` (only C9, shifted, is left); `Attack.claw` (the base-variant path removed; check mode asserts the claw's W9 against a listed entry); `Attack.hit` (slot (97 r) >> 15 and its check); `P` (WDIG of 15,520 words); `k4q` (the claw's W9; mates among the group's classes); `k4f` (the diagnostic over the four groups of `_k4ind`); `_k4fin` (planes of one group from its prefix set); `k4_budget` (G and the second-order divisor 1 - 0.07579); `_e1` (transplant-claw: advice checks and the fibre checks per group; random transplants with a listed entry); `_k4e` (no base F8 count; the acceptance constants). Removed: `_w3gen`, `_k4c1`, `_sm`. Added: `_k4st`, `_k4fe`, `_k4lf`, `_k4cls`, `_k4build`, `_k4ind`, `h4ok`. Every other routine is byte-identical to w13's.

## 7. Success probability and the cap
- **Trials.** A trial is a distinct (a2, kappa) key with at least one listed entry passing F8, in a claw passing F9. Mates of a key share W17 and differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W8 and every tail word from W18 on (Section 2.4). When a key hits W17 the program tests every class of its group, so every mate passing F8 is compressed; the key succeeds if any of them does, so with probability at least that of any one of them. No independence and no other relation between the tails of mates is used.
- **Count: 8956.4 per distinct claw.** On 2,000 real F9 claws of the shipped program (16 batches of 125: the first 125 F9 claws, in arrival order, of windows 1000 to 1015) the distinct keys with an entry in F8 number 576,745.3 per F9 claw (s.e. 970.3 from the batch means; per-claw s.d. 57,687). Times 898.625 distinct F9 claws per window (48 windows), divided by 57,010.58: 9090.904 trials per distinct claw (s.e. 51.689). One-sided 99% lower bound, estimate - 2.602 x s.e. with t(15) = 2.602: 8956.409, priced as 8956.4. Counted by w15/tools/f8count.exe over the exhaustive list, which equals the rule set (Section 2.5). Taking the first claws of a window is not a selection on the count: on all F9 claws of windows 1000 and 1001 the first 125 average 580,014 and 576,395 keys against 577,913 and 574,102 for the rest (Welch z = +0.39, +0.40). Observation, not a premise and not priced: the same claws have 682,518.4 F8-passing entries per F9 claw, 1.1834 per key. Window 1000 is also the window on which the fibre was compared with its neighbours (in an earlier build of the walk, 908 claws there); its 125 claws are 1/16 of this sample and their mean, 580,014 keys, lies within the spread of the other windows (one-way ANOVA over the 16 windows: F = 0.564 on 15 and 1,984 df, between-window s.d. estimated 0).

- **Success: second-order Bonferroni over all key hits (counting every hit, as a7b383d1 does; credited for that only).** (i) The program tests every W17 key hit of every window: `k4q` (experiments/r39joint_k4.py lines 1027-1042) runs over every survivor lane of every group, and at each key hit compresses every class of the group whose words pass W9, W17 and F8 (lines 1035-1041, 560 per class and 2 x 2,812 per compressed pair, inside the window's counted work and priced in K as key-hit work); after a hit without collision the loops continue, and a window stops early only on a collision (line 789). At most m_max = 1,024 distinct F9 claws are evaluated per window (`k4d`, line 1091). (ii) For a trial key k let its designated mate be its lowest-a3 class whose entry passes F8 in the claw, and B_k the event that the designated mate's pair collides; B_k is contained in the key's success, because the program compresses every mate, and p'_k = P(B_k | claws). (iii) Given the hits, the window succeeds with probability at least P(union over hit k of B_k) >= sum over hits of p'_k - sum over hit pairs k < l of P(B_k and B_l) (second-order Bonferroni, for any number H of hits). Each pair term is at most min(p'_k, p'_l) <= (p'_k + p'_l) / 2, whatever the joint law of the tails, so the pair sum is at most sum over hit k of p'_k x (number of other hit keys) / 2. The designated-mate events are used, not the key's whole success event: the coefficient is negative for H >= 4, so the measured lower bound may be substituted only where the probability itself is the designated mate's, which arm K measures. (iv) Average over the hits given the claws (H5): each trial key is hit with probability q = 2^-32; keys of different claws are hit independently; inside one claw W17 = G(a2, kappa, w) + c(claw) with w and c fixed by the claw, so two keys of a claw are hit together exactly when their G values coincide, which the program-independent count sweep/cohit.c measures at 1.336 times the independent pair rate (512 random w, all 3,462,264 keys). Hence E[pair sum | claws] <= sum over k of p'_k [q^2 (n_w - D_c(k)) + q pi_k] / 2, with D_c(k) the trial keys of k's claw and pi_k its expected co-hit partners in that claw. The cross-claw part is q^2 sum over claws c of P_c (m_w - 1) mu_D after averaging the other claws' key counts, which are functions of their own (a0, a1) only and i.i.d. across the claws of a window (H1): since m_w <= m_max by the program, it is at most q^2 (m_max - 1) mu_D P_w for ANY dependence between the number of claws and the tails, with mu_D <= 579,271 (the 99% bound, rounded up of the keys per claw, 576,745 + 2.602 x 970). Within a claw, both keys of a pair hit iff their G values coincide. The Bonferroni sum is taken over the sub-collection of hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has at most 4 keys; a union over fewer events is still a lower bound, and the choice depends on the claw's (w, c) only, not on any tail. For a kept key N_k(w) <= 3, so its pair term is (q/2) p'_k min(N_k(w), 3). Averaged over w (independent of the tails, H5) it is at most (q/2) p'_k pi_max with pi_max = 1.36e-2, the family-wise bound (alpha = 0.001, all keys, two runs of 16,384 random w: 1.3556e-02 and 1.3355e-02) on E[min(N_k, 3)] for every listed key. The left-out hits lose at most q p'_k P(N_k >= 4) of the first-order term, with P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3,462,264 / 0.001) / 16,384 = 0.001341 for every key (no N >= 4 for any key in 16,384 w; family-wise at alpha = 0.001). Participant tools: w15/sweep/cohit2.c (output w15/sweep/cohit2_16384.txt), w15/sweep/cohit3.c (w15/sweep/cohit3_16384.txt), w15/sweep/nf.c (w15/sweep/nf.txt: s0(y) - y has at most 14 preimages, so N_k(w) <= 2,799; not needed by the bound). Both terms are bounded for every key, so they hold whatever the correlation between partner rates and tails across keys. c2 = 2^-32 x 1,023 x 579,271 / 2 + 1.36e-2 / 2 = 0.068988 + 0.006800 = 0.075788, and the divisor is 1 - c2 - 0.001341 = 1 - 0.077129. No moment of the window size, no correlation and no allowance enters. Over windows, E[q P_w] = E[n_w] q p_key with p_key the designated-mate tail weighted by trial keys (H2-transfer; arm K weighted by window size). (v) Windows are independent (fresh first blocks): P(no success) <= product over windows of (1 - P(window success)) <= exp(-lambda). No hit is selected or ordered; every hit enters symmetrically; the bound holds for any dependence between the tails of different hits. Hence lambda = B x G x 8956.4 x 2^-32 x 2^-74.3238 x (1 - 0.077129) = -ln 0.61 + 2^-40, set in `k4_budget`; success 0.39. The pair term costs 0.1137 bit. (vi) Real W17 hits at probability 2^-32 were observed: the 48 windows had 37 key hits against 38.58 expected over all 200 groups (dispersion chi-square 34.35 on 47 df); of them, 3 F8-passing mates were compressed against 6.85 expected (Poisson P = 0.09, adverse and not significant; disclosed).
- **The cap does not bind (H6).** Each sample moment replaced by its one-sided 99.75% bound (Bonferroni, four together at 99%): walk mean t(23) = 3.104, s.d. by chi-square 8.450 on 23 df; F9 count t(47) = 2.946, chi-square 24.316 on 47 df. Mean work: 605,977,191 per window against the cap 10,719 x 57,010.58 = 611,096,407: margin 5,119,217, 0.84% of the cap (1.66% at the sample moments). Per-window s.d. at most 14,621,707 (walk, F9 count x 144,930, survivors, and the key hit with probability 0.8166 per window at 49,472), summed with no independence assumed. Chebyshev over B windows: below 7.7e-23.
- **The claw cap never binds in the measured windows.** At most 969 distinct F9 claws were evaluated in any of the 48 windows and at most 11 in the organizer windows, below m_max = 1,024, so every k4d call there took the same branch with the same charge as without the cap, and the 48 windows and the organizer tuples are the shipped program's own. The claw factor in the trial count is the sample mean of min(m_w, 1,024) over the 48 windows, a direct measurement of the capped program's quantity; it equals the printed F9 mean because no window reached the cap (maximum 969), and its s.e. is the one carried into the trial bound. **The last window.** The cap is checked between windows; one window's k4 work is at most 1,024 x (143,633 + 62,400 x (5,215 + 49,472)) operations by the cap (every lane a survivor with 8 classes and a key hit), and its walk work was at most 476,731,245 operations in the 48 windows; even a walk part 1,000 times that keeps one window under 2^42 operations, 2^42 / 2,812 compressions, which is added to the total charged work (Section 5) and to the program's time assertion.

## 8. The tail (replica of 5f8e6192, run by the organizer; priced under the MODEL premise H2-transfer)
- `experiments/r39tail.py` is w13's file, byte-identical: the replica with QDECL = -74.54, run by the organizer as r39-tail-01..14. Its hard asserts and the 42 further runs behind the check value QDECL are those of w13 Section 8 (14-run mean 2^-74.3238; 42 further runs, mean 2^-74.4434, one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5296).
- **This entry prices the tail at 2^-74.3238 under the declared MODEL premise H2-transfer.** The value is the linear mean of the 14 organizer-executed runs r39-tail-01..14, hard-asserted by the unchanged replica, which sample the advice draws; the premise takes it for the designated mate on the fibre 0x3cc9eebe. It is a new, favorable declared heuristic of this entry, not inherited from 5f8e6192's acceptance, offered under the exploratory lane's standard for declared heuristics with relevant evidence (JUDGE_LANES.md, lines 55-65). Relevant evidence, below: the paired transfer arm (-0.014 bit, s.e. 0.023); the new-fibre arms K (key-weighted, mean 2^-74.3734, s.e. 0.0364) and R 3cc9eebe (mean 2^-74.3781, s.e. 0.0289) lie 0.0496 and 0.0543 bit below the priced value. The replica's check value QDECL = -74.54 is unchanged; pricing at it instead would add 0.2162 bit. 0b62ed88's further runs, recomputed from the run files of w13 (build/tail15.py):

| runs of the replica | verified collisions | mean | one-sided 99% bound | one-sided 99.9% bound |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

The check value QDECL = -74.54 lies 0.0104 bit under the one-sided 99.9% bound of the 42 runs and under the mean of each set of 14. Local against organizer-protocol runs: Welch t = -2.62 on the run values; QDECL rests on all 42 runs pooled.
- **Transfer to the variants of the new fibre (MEASURED by this entry's previous seat, participant-run, not organizer-executed; w15/tail, re-analysed here).** The organizer's replica r39-tail-01..14 samples W8 in F8 and W9 in F9 on the advice values of W10, W11, not the new fibre's class-01 entries. Joint arms replace W8..W11 per lane by real words: R arms take (claw, entry) uniformly over F8-passing pairs on real F9 claws (w13 windows for h0, windows of the shifted walk for 3cc9eebe; every claw asserted in F9 under its fibre); S arms take W9, W8 from their filters and (W10, W11) from a uniform entry. The R arm weights entries uniformly; the attack's trials are keys. The key-weighted arm K below measures the attack's quantity directly. Every arm on the organizer seed protocol (ids r39-tail-15..42 for R, 15..28 for S), with the identical SMC carrier for equal ids, so paired differences cancel the carrier; every hit verified by recompressing both blocks.

| arm | runs | verified hits | log2 linear mean | s.e. |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

- Paired, R 3cc9eebe - R h0 over 28 runs: log2 ratio of linear means -0.014 (s.e. 0.023); pooled hits -0.0105 (Poisson s.e. 0.0181). One-sided 99% bound on the loss: -0.014 - 2.473 x 0.023 = -0.071 bit, so a loss above 0.071 bit is excluded at 99%. Sensitivity: in the attack every trial has a0 even and W1 odd (class 01); the pool arms back-solve W1 with either parity, and the class-01-only paired figure is -0.021. Real variants of either fibre do not do worse than the shipped draws (R 3cc9eebe - adv: +0.023, s.e. 0.032). Row survival 25/24, 26/25, 27/26, 28/27 equal within noise. - **Key-weighted arm K (participant-run, w15/tail/mkpoolk.c, armk.sh, analyzek.py).** Per proposal: a claw drawn uniformly from the F9 claws of window 1000 + i - 15 of the shipped program (run i), and a distinct (a2, kappa) key drawn uniformly from the list, kept if the key has a mate passing F8 in that claw; the proposed words are those of its designated mate, the lowest-a3 class passing F8 (ascending a3 is the order in which k4q tests them). So (claw, key) is uniform over the pairs in which the key is a trial, as the hit keys of the attack are (every trial key is hit with the same probability 2^-32), and the proposal is the designated mate's pair, which the program compresses at every hit of that key; no reweighting and no premise on mates. Same ids r39-tail-15..42, same SMC carrier as R, every hit verified and its (a0..a3) recovered. Result: mean 2^-74.3734, one-sided 99% bound 2^-74.4662, **one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5035** (Student t, 27 df, 3.421); class-01 only (2 x c01) 2^-74.3528, its 99.9% bound 2^-74.4887. Weighted by the number of evaluated claws of each run's window (the attack weights windows by their trials): mean 2^-74.3747, one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5058; correlation of window size and run tail -0.19. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1). Paired against the entry-weighted R arm (same carrier): +0.0047 bit (s.e. 0.0172). Accepted keys had 1.1857 F8-passing mates on average in the first run.

**Transfer to the new fibre.** Priced directly on the new fibre, the R 3cc9eebe arm alone (28 runs, mean -74.3781) has the one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.4804 (Student t, 27 df, 3.421), above the replica's check value 2^-74.54. The R-arm claws came from windows of the shifted walk of an earlier build (previous seat's tools; seed 1000 gave 908 F9 claws there against 871 in the shipped program's window 1000), so the arm uses real F9 claws of the same walk map but not the shipped program's own windows. The figure that matches the attack exactly would be the class-01-only paired one, and it is inside the same bound.

## 9. Advice construction and preprocessing (H3)
As in w13 Section 9: the pair of 5f8e6192, chosen among 93 candidate pairs; 93 x 2^36 = 2^42.5392 constructions plus 93 x 14 x 2^24 = 2^34.35 screens, 2^42.545 in all, declared as preprocessing_log2 = 43 and added to the claimed time. The organizer experiment runs the fibre search on the shipped pair (g16_fibre_size = 2, g17_fibre_size = 1, fibre_dfs_ops = 1,944) and the 256-candidate slice (advice_slice_hits = 1, ops_per_cand = 411). The list is built at import inside K4_SETUP; the choice of the fibre is a one-time offline search: about 7,000 fibres scored (at most 2^36 operations), five enumerated exhaustively by enum15 (per fibre 2^32 F11 tests of about 20 operations, 2^36.3, plus the real two-message trail at four points on at most 1.8 x 10^8 F10-passing solutions at about 10^3 operations each, 2^39.4; five fibres 2^41.8), their F8 counts on about 950 real claws each (9.7 x 10^6 entries x 50 operations per claw, 2^38.7 each, 2^41.0 for five) and one window per fibre: at most 2^42.6 operations, 2^31.1 compressions in all (EST from the tools' loop counts), against the 2^41.1 compressions left between the 2^42.545 of the advice and the declared 2^43.

## 10. Premises, and the limits of their evidence
- **H1-claw-model.** First-block chaining values behave as independent uniform values; the (a0, a1) of the distinct F9 claws of a window are i.i.d., independent of the chaining value and of the number of claws; the trial-key count of a claw is a function of its (a0, a1) only (W8..W11, hence F8, do not depend on the chaining value); one-way ANOVA of the 2,000 claws' key counts over their 16 windows: F = 0.564 on 15 and 1,984 df. Survivors per evaluated claw at most 0.23995; walk work and yield as in Section 5.
- **H1-ops.** The constants of Section 5; the pass is a constant of the program.
- **H2-transfer (MODEL, declared, favorable; new in this entry).** p_tail >= 2^-74.3238 for the designated (lowest-a3) F8 mate of a trial key drawn uniformly over all trial (window, claw, key) triples of the attack, so windows weighted by their trial count, in a claw passing F9 with W17 hit: the linear mean of the 14 organizer runs r39-tail-01..14 on the advice draws, carried to the fibre 0x3cc9eebe. Evidence: the paired transfer arm (-0.014 bit, s.e. 0.023); arm K (mean 2^-74.3734, s.e. 0.0364; weighted by window size, one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5058) and arm R 3cc9eebe (mean 2^-74.3781), participant-run, both below the priced value. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier of the arm sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1); the words W0..W7 of the chaining value are free in it, as in every earlier tail arm.
- **H3-advice-construction.** As in w13; for every listed entry of the new fibre both messages follow the advice trail through step 15 (enum15 on all entries; the organizer run on one entry of every group).
- **H5-group-independence.** Windows independent; trials are distinct keys with an entry in F8, at least 8956.4 per distinct claw; each listed key's W17 event has probability 2^-32 in each claw; events of different claws are independent. Within a claw, two keys hit together iff G(a2, kappa, w) = s0(a2 + w) - (a2 + w) + kappa coincide. Let N_k(w) be the number of other listed keys with G equal to key k's at the claw's w, and pi_k = E_w[N_k(w)]. Measured over all 3,462,264 listed keys on two independent sets of 16,384 random w: mean pi 1.07e-3, largest per-key estimate 4.6e-3; per-(key, w) counts on the second set: N = 1 in 60,723,478 cases, N = 2 in 37,173, N = 3 in 40, N >= 4 in none of 5.67e10. At the w of 2,000 real F9 claws of the shipped program: mean pi 1.0825e-3, largest per-(key, w) N = 3 (w15/critic_final/cohit_real.c, cohit_real_2000.txt; w and u at all 43,134 real claws in wreal.py, wreal.txt). The claw's w contains -cv5 additively, so it is uniform and independent of (a0, u) under H1. Hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has more than 4 keys are left out of the second-order sum; for every kept key N_k <= 3, and family-wise over all keys (alpha = 0.001) E[min(N_k, 3)] <= 1.36e-2. Left-out hits cost at most P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3,462,264 / 0.001) / 16,384 = 1.341e-3 per key in the first-order term (no N >= 4 for any key in 16,384 w; family-wise over all keys at alpha = 0.001). Both bounds hold for every key, so the within-claw term holds whatever the relation between a key's partner rate and its tail. The claw's W17 constants (w, c) are independent of the designated-mate tail events, as for the hit events themselves. 37 real 2^-32 key hits were observed against 38.58 expected (Section 7).
- **H6-cap-completion.** Section 7.
- **H-implicit-distinct-key-dispersion.** Tested in the organizer run at a scaled event over all keys of four groups in every F9 claw (Section 11).
- **Limits of the evidence.** The walk and F9 samples are 24 and 48 windows of the shipped program on public seeds, and the trial count is our 2,000 claws: participant-run. The organizer run counts F8-passing keys and their scaled dispersion on four fixed groups of the 200 (22 claws); it is a spot test at probability 2^-7 and does not establish independence of the 2^-32 events over all groups and all windows, which remains the premise H5. The tail replica the organizer runs samples the advice distribution; the transfer to the new fibre rests on the participant-run 28-run arms (paired -0.014, s.e. 0.023; direct 99.9% bound 2^-74.4804 on the new fibre). The memory claim is a peak over phases. No full collision has been executed; every experiment is a component test.

## 11. Experiments (organizer sandbox; every organizer-run value is hard-asserted by the program)
- `r39-transplant-claw`, trial 0: the advice collides under 39 steps; the advice-construction checks of Section 9; and for the sample entry of each of the 200 groups at the advice point: the rule holds, W9 = advice W9 + 0x05cefde0, W16 one value, both messages follow the advice trail through step 16 and message 1 the advice states from A[8], E[12] (200 of 200). Every further trial: a random chaining value and claw-free (a0, u) with a listed entry of the fibre: transplant states, W1 = u and W16 - g = F(u) - F(a0).
- `r39k4-window-small`, trials 0-3: windows of 2^21 evaluations, check mode, k4 on for every F9 claw (7, 11, 4, 1 claws). Every claw asserts W9 = C9 + HD - a1 = W9 of a listed entry and W16 = g. The pass runs over all 62,400 lanes. Asserted tuples (claws, F9, 0, pass lanes, survivors, key hits, k4 ops, total ops): (233,7,0,436800,2,0,1019221,11504962), (222,11,0,624000,5,0,1454268,13875066), (256,4,0,249600,2,0,584630,13031225), (232,1,0,62400,0,0,144113,11245985). Each k4 ops value is (evaluated F9 claws, pass lanes / 62,400) x (143,633 + 480), plus 12 per repeated F9 claw (the dedupe lookup), plus 10,430 for its 2 real survivors; 13,126 for its 5 real survivors; 8,178 for its 2 real survivors. Each trial emits k4_setup = 1,107,473,556.
  - Pass-off control: trials 0 and 1 are re-run with k4 off; claws and F9 equal, ops_off = ops - k4_ops.
  - Planted check on the first F9 claw of each window, for each of the 200 groups: the key is found and its counted cost is asserted.
  - Key dispersion over all entries of every 50th group (4 groups), all F9 claws: per claw D = keys with an entry in F8, K = those whose W17 x 2654435761 mod 2^32 has its top 7 bits zero (probability 2^-7). Asserted per trial (sum D, sum K, Pearson, claws): (59,256, 437, 6.5188, 7); (67,492, 518, 7.9839, 10); (17,882, 142, 0.7772, 4); (1,872, 7, 4.0067, 1). Pooled 146,502 key events, 1,104 hits against 1144.5 expected (z = -1.20), Pearson 19.29 on 22 claws. Acceptance region, asserted on the sums: sum D >= 96,821, |sum K - sum D/128| within 2.576 s.d., Pearson < 40.29 (99% quantile, 22 dof).
- `r39-tail-01..14`: the replica with QDECL = -74.54, unchanged.
- Local seed sets, run by this entry with the same program and code path: 11 sets of 4 windows with seeds fixed before any run (sha256 of `w15-dispersion|setNN|i`), 138 claws, 6,693 hits against 6675.6 expected (z = +0.21), Pearson 126.68 on 138 degrees of freedom; the largest set value is z = +1.43. On the organizer seeds the largest per-claw |z| is 2.00.

Linux (WSL) wall time of each experiment in the organizer form, three passes: at most 9.0 s.
